newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Bank of East Asia to open Taiwan branch.
newsitem.headline: HK's Bank of East Asia to open Taiwan branch.

text.p: Hong Kong-based Bank of East Asia Ltd (BEA) plans to open its first Taiwan branch in the first half of 1997, deputy chairman David Li said on Thursday.
"We anticipate that our new Taipei branch will commence business in the first half of 1997," Li told reporters, adding that the branch would receive an injection of more than NT$150 million.
BEA currently operates six branches and five representative offices in mainland China.
Li said BEA applied for permission in December 1994 to open the Taiwan branch and was granted approval by the Taiwan Finance Ministry on October 16.
It had to demonstrate that mainland Chinese shareholder interest in the bank did not exceed a ceiling set by Taipei.
"They were concerned about how much mainland interest is in the Bank of East Asia because there is a ruling in Taipei that no mainland (investors) can have more than 20 percent," Li said.
Taiwan has banned direct official links with China since Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists lost the civil war and fled to the island in 1949.

Mainland shareholder interest, which includes shareholders who lodged shares with nominee companies in the Bank of China group or other mainland China groups, has not exceeded 11.6 percent over a sustained period of time.
